items.title: Madagascar: dix ans de gestion des finances publiques passés au crible dans un rapport

original_payload.original_title: Madagascar: dix ans de gestion des finances publiques passés au crible dans un rapport
original_payload.original_body:
Madagascar: dix ans de gestion des finances publiques passés au crible dans un rapport
À Madagascar, un rapport produit conjointement par le ministère de l’Économie et des Finances, l’Union européenne et l’Agence française de développement (AFD) passe au peigne fin la gestion des finances publiques au cours des dix dernières années. Présenté jeudi 26 novembre à Antananarivo, il pointe une série d’améliorations, mais aussi de nombreuses failles dans le fonctionnement de la machine étatique : retards de paiement, surestimation des rentrées fiscales, méconnaissance du patrimoine de l’État. À partir de ce diagnostic, l’objectif fixé consiste à moderniser et à sécuriser la gestion des finances publiques.
Mettre RFI en favori sur Google
pour voir les contenus de RFI s’afficher en priorité dans vos résultats de recherche.
Publié le :  28/11/2026 - 04:37
3 min     Temps de lecture
Les participants à l'atelier de restitution sur la gestion des finances publiques, le vendredi 27 novembre 2026 à Antananarivo.        © Guilhem Fabry / RFI
Par :
RFI
Publicité
Avec notre correspondant à Antananarivo,   Guilhem Fabry
Le rapport pointe des avancées : 90 % des taxes douanières sont collectées en ligne et le nombre de contribuables malgaches est passé de 272 769 en 2017 à plus de 1,59 million en 2026. Mais les projets d’investissement manquent d’analyse   économique   préalable, les administrations fonctionnent en « silo », sans partager leurs données, et la valeur exacte du patrimoine de l’État demeure méconnue.
Les prévisions budgétaires sont par ailleurs peu fiables, de l’aveu même du secrétaire général du ministère de l’Économie et des   Finances  , Iouri Garisse Razafindrakoto.
«  On a une certaine tendance à surestimer les recettes. On a toutes sortes de services compétents pour mener à bien ce genre d’exercice. Mais les pressions politiques et macroéconomiques les contraignent à accepter de produire des prévisions qui ne sont pas si réalistes que ça. C’est un vrai chantier, de faire en sorte que ces techniciens puissent dire à tous les décideurs que ce qu’on est en train de mettre dans les prévisions n’est pas réaliste. Quand les recettes sont surestimées, à la fin de l’année on aura du mal à exécuter convenablement le budget. Il faut bien qu’il soit équilibré, certaines dépenses seront donc coupées ou bien reportées pour les exercices suivants  », explique-t-il.
«  Les exercices d’appréciation de l’appareil administratif sont très importants. Cela permet une mise en exergue pour les techniciens, mais c’est aussi un message pour tous les décideurs : si quelque chose ne fonctionne pas très bien, il faut en tenir compte  », ajoute Iouri Garisse Razafindrakoto.
À lire aussi  Madagascar: le projet de loi de finances 2026 arrive à l'Assemblée nationale
Un enjeu de confiance et de réputation internationale
Améliorer la fiabilité et la transparence des finances publiques est une condition pour rétablir la confiance des citoyens dans l’État, rappelle-t-il, alors que la Cour des comptes a pointé, en début d’année, les dérives du régime déchu. Roland Kobia, ambassadeur de l’Union européenne à   Madagascar  , soulève, lui, un autre enjeu.
«  Nous sommes en discussion sur toute une série de dossiers sur la lutte contre la corruption, sur le blanchiment d’argent, sur la lutte contre le terrorisme. L’exercice s’inscrit dans cette logique de consolidation des ressources financières de l'État, de consolidation de la réputation internationale de Madagascar pour éviter que Madagascar ne verse dans certaines listes qui pourraient être au détriment de son action financière et économique.  »
Une référence à la liste grise du Gafi, le Groupe d’action financière, chargé de la lutte contre le blanchiment. Un éventuel placement de Madagascar sous surveillance renforcée refroidirait les investisseurs étrangers.

items.title: FG to inaugurate new Abeokuta transmission substation in March 2027

original_payload.original_title: FG to inaugurate new Abeokuta transmission substation in March 2027
original_payload.original_body:
Oil & Gas  FG to inaugurate new Abeokuta transmission substation in March 2027
By  Folashade Adeniran   ·   5 hours ago   ·  3 min read
✓
✓
By Abiodun Lawal
The Minister of Power, Mr Joseph Tegbe, says the new Abeokuta Transmission Substation project will be inaugurated in March.
Tegbe gave the assurance on Friday in Abeokuta after inspecting the ongoing project, describing the level of work achieved as encouraging.
The minister said the project was at an advanced stage, adding that most equipment had been installed, while the remaining components required installation and testing.
According to him, the facility is expected to undergo cold commissioning in December, followed by hot commissioning and energisation, before full commissioning in March 2027.
“The Abeokuta facility is among five substations being developed under batch one of the transmission expansion programme.
“Other locations include: Ayede in Oyo, Sokoto, Ofa in Kwara and Onitsha. The projects will collectively add 986 megawatts to the country’s transmission capacity,” he said.
Tegbe further explained that the projects were part of the Federal Government’s efforts to strengthen electricity transmission and improve access to reliable power nationwide.
He explained that increasing generation without adequate transmission and distribution infrastructure would continue to constrain electricity supply.
The minister disclosed that he would also meet with four distribution companies, including Abuja, Ikeja, Eko and Ibadan, to address challenges affecting electricity delivery.
He said the government was adopting a coordinated approach involving gas suppliers, generating companies, the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Ltd. and relevant ministries.
Tegbe said the approach was designed to address challenges across the electricity value chain, from gas supply and generation to transmission, distribution and final consumers.
On the Federal Government’s $1trillion economy target, Tegbe described electricity as fundamental to industrialisation, economic growth and national prosperity.
He said Nigeria was targeting 10,000 megawatts of electricity generation by 2031, alongside transmission capacity of at least 19,000 megawatts.
Tegbe said the targets would strengthen electricity supply to commercial and industrial consumers and provide the foundation for achieving the country’s economic ambition.
Also, the Managing Director , FGN Power Company, Mr Kenny Anuwe, said the ongoing upgrade of the new Abeokuta substation would inject an additional 480 megawatts into Ogun state’s industrial corridor.
He explained that the flagship PPI phase one, batch one project was transforming the existing 132/33kV facility into a modern 330/132/33kV substation within an 18-month timeline.
“The upgraded facility will improve power evacuation, strengthen network reliability, and meet rising electricity demand for industrial development, commercial enterprises, and residential consumers.
“The Presidential Power Initiative represents a strategic Federal Government intervention designed to resolve longstanding infrastructure bottlenecks across Nigeria’s generation, transmission, and distribution value chain,” he said.
He emphasised that beyond infrastructure expansion, the initiative remained a core pillar of the government’s broader economic growth and industrialisation agenda aimed at boosting national productivity.
Anuwe, while highlighting milestones achieved with Siemens Energy, said the PPI pilot phase delivered 10 power transformers and 10 mobile substations, adding about 1,080MW wheeling capacity nationwide.
He reaffirmed FGN Power Company’s commitment to coordinating stakeholders and translating PPI objectives into measurable electricity improvements nationwide.
He thanked the Minister of Power for his sustained guidance.(NAN)www.nannews.ng

items.title: Moyen-Chari : 250 femmes en formation aux techniques agricoles à Moussafoyo

original_payload.original_title: Moyen-Chari : 250 femmes en formation aux techniques agricoles à Moussafoyo
original_payload.original_body:
250 femmes de la sous-préfecture de Moussafoyo, dans le département du Barh-Koh, bénéficient, depuis le 25 novembre 2026, d’une formation sur les techniques de production agricole et la gestion financière simplifiée. Cette initiative est organisée par l’Association pour la promotion du développement durable et intégral (APDI), avec l’appui du Fonds canadien d’initiative locale (FCIL).
Après avoir reçu des intrants et plusieurs équipements agricoles, les bénéficiaires renforcent désormais leurs connaissances afin de mieux exploiter ces moyens de production. Pendant quatre jours, elles apprendront les différentes étapes nécessaires à la conduite d’une activité agricole, depuis le choix du terrain jusqu’à la récolte.
Les séances portent notamment sur la préparation du sol, la sélection des semences adaptées, le respect des périodes de semis et les bonnes pratiques culturales. La formation aborde également la gestion de l’argent, la tenue d’une caisse, l’épargne et l’élaboration d’un budget, afin de permettre aux participantes de mieux organiser leurs activités génératrices de revenus.
Lire aussi :  Moyen-Chari : 250 femmes de Moussafoyo bénéficient de semences améliorées
Pour le coordonnateur de l’APDI, Yamba Ruben, l’augmentation des récoltes passe par l’adoption de bonnes pratiques agricoles. Il estime que le choix de variétés adaptées, le respect du calendrier agricole et une bonne préparation des parcelles sont indispensables pour obtenir de meilleurs résultats.
« À travers cette formation, nous entendons améliorer les compétences des productrices afin d’accroître les rendements, de préserver la qualité des récoltes et de renforcer la rentabilité de leurs exploitations », a-t-il déclaré.
Lire aussi :  Moyen-Chari : à l’approche des récoltes, l’ADESPM renforce la prévention des conflits dans le canton Moussafoyo
Dès cette première journée, certaines participantes sont passées à la pratique, notamment à travers des exercices de sarclage.
Cette formation vient ainsi compléter l’appui matériel déjà accordé aux bénéficiaires de Moussafoyo, avec pour ambition de rendre leurs activités agricoles plus productives.

original_payload.original_body:
Several cities in Peru and Ecuador are facing major flooding after downpours in the region linked to an exceptionally strong  El Nino .
In the city of Piura, capital of the Piura region in northern Peru, waist-high water filled the streets following 12 hours of heavy rains that began on Thursday.

Some 2,000 families have been affected by the rains in Piura, according to preliminary reports, National Institute of Civil Defense chief Luis Vasquez told the RPP radio station.
“This is just the first heavy rain from the El Nino phenomenon and look at how it’s treating us,” said resident Pierre Garavito, as a refrigerator bobbed in the water inside his home in Piura’s Santa Margarita neighbourhood.
“I’ve lost everything … This is how all the residents in the neighbourhood are,” he said.
Floodwaters forced authorities to relocate patients from the ward for respiratory infections at Piura’s Jose Cayetano Heredia Hospital to its auditorium. Patients in more serious condition were transferred to intensive care.
The flooding also affected the Plaza de Armas in central Piura, along with many businesses and public buildings.

items.title: Parts of US clean up after Thanksgiving storm lashes East Coast

original_payload.original_title: Parts of US clean up after Thanksgiving storm lashes East Coast
original_payload.original_body:
Heavy rain and flooding have begun to ease along the US East Coast as power is being slowly restored to hundreds of thousands of customers following a round of holiday storms.
The storms disrupted travel and downed trees and power lines, leading to water rescues in multiple states, from New York to Virginia.
Recommended Stories

list 2 of 3  As tech outages mount, some New Yorkers prepare for the worst
list 3 of 3  Why does Elon Musk want to put a million satellite data centres in space?
end of list
In New York City, preparations were under way for the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade on Saturday after an  unprecedented postponement  because of rain and high winds.
The parade, an annual spectacle usually held on Thanksgiving Day, sees brightly coloured balloons travel through the heart of Manhattan. The festivities also kick off the holiday shopping season for the US.
The same balloons and floats, and most of the original celebrities, are still set to take part, organisers said.
Elsewhere, wet snow fell as far south as the Tennessee Valley and freezing rain moved across northern New England. Cold rain was reported in parts of the Midwest, including the Ohio Valley and the lower Great Lakes.
While conditions are expected to improve across the entire eastern US, the National Weather Service warned that “this huge system will take some time to weaken”.
The low-pressure system that brought the storm to the East Coast, the service added, would continue to slowly exit to the northeast, “bringing lingering showers and isolated freezing precipitation through Saturday”.
Coastal flood warnings were also issued in several states from New Jersey to Virginia.
Power restored, travel disruptions ease
The number of power outages, which  peaked on Thursday at more than 900,000 , fell to 264,000 by Friday evening as crews worked to restore electricity, according to poweroutage.us.

items.title: Ligue des champions : comment Canal+ a réduit les émissions de CO2 de la retransmission de PSG–Roma

original_payload.original_body:

L’UEFA chiffre à près de trois tonnes de CO2 les économies réalisées sur l’alimentation électrique et la restauration lors du match de mercredi au Parc des Princes.
Europe Sport      Par  Rodrigue Kévin Adjovi
·   28 Nov. 2026 à 04:15  28/11/26 04:15       ·   2 min  de lecture

Partager
Ajouter Bénin Web TV à vos sources préférées
Canal+ a testé un dispositif de production télévisuelle visant à réduire ses émissions de CO2 à l’occasion du match de Ligue des champions entre le Paris Saint-Germain et l’AS Rome, mercredi 25 novembre. L’UEFA a présenté vendredi les premiers résultats de cette expérimentation menée avec le diffuseur, le PSG et les responsables du Parc des Princes.
Le principal changement a concerné les installations techniques. Grâce à des travaux réalisés dans le stade parisien, les équipes ont pu privilégier le raccordement au réseau électrique français plutôt que les groupes électrogènes fonctionnant au carburant.
Les déplacements ont aussi été revus. Le train a été privilégié pour rejoindre Paris, puis les transports collectifs et le covoiturage pour accéder au stade. Sur place, la restauration a fait appel à des produits locaux et de saison, sans viande rouge. Les repas non consommés ont été redistribués.
Selon le bilan publié par l’UEFA, les seules mesures portant sur l’électricité et les repas ont permis d’éviter l’émission de près de trois tonnes de CO2 par rapport à un dispositif habituel. L’organisme n’a pas communiqué de bilan chiffré global de la retransmission.
Thomas Sénécal, directeur des sports de Canal+, souhaite tirer les enseignements de cet essai pour les futures productions sportives du groupe. Il n’a pas annoncé de calendrier de généralisation.
Le groupe a par ailleurs annoncé le 4 août dernier l’acquisition des droits exclusifs des compétitions européennes de clubs en Afrique subsaharienne pour quatre saisons à partir de mi-2027, dans plus de 40 pays. Rien n’indique à ce stade que le dispositif testé à Paris sera déployé sur l’ensemble de ces retransmissions.
Sur le terrain,  Paris et Rome ont fait match nul (2-2)  lors de cette cinquième journée de la phase de ligue.

items.title: Africa: COP31 - New African Development Bank Report Calls for Climate Finance That Promotes Peace

original_payload.original_title: Africa: COP31 - New African Development Bank Report Calls for Climate Finance That Promotes Peace
original_payload.original_body:
Climate and development finance for Africa's fragile and conflict-affected settings must be designed from the outset to prevent conflict and strengthen social cohesion.
This is, according to a new African Development Bank Group report launched at the 31st Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (COP31) in Antalya, Türkiye on 18 November 2026.
Titled  Advancing the Climate-Peace Agenda: Mobilising Climate Finance for Conflict Prevention, Resilience and Peacebuilding in Africa , the report was jointly prepared by the Bank's Transition States Coordination Office and its Climate Change and Green Growth Department, in consultation with partners including the African Union, ODI Global, the International Committee of the Red Cross, the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute (SIPRI), the International Organization for Migration (IOM), the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), the World Food Programme (WFP) and the Islamic Development Bank.
The report highlights a significant imbalance. Africa contributes less than 4% of global carbon dioxide emissions, yet climate vulnerability increasingly overlaps with fragility, conflict, food insecurity and displacement. Fragile and conflict-affected contexts received only about US$10 per person a year in adaptation finance between 2014 and 2021, compared with about US$161 elsewhere. Africa's annual adaptation needs exceed US$70 billion, against about US$14.8 billion in tracked adaptation finance.
To address this, the report calls for a paradigm shift to go beyond "do no harm" and conflict sensitivity towards intentional, peace-positive investment. "Climate finance in fragile settings must be designed for peace from the start, by asking who benefits, who is excluded and how each investment strengthens social cohesion," said  Yero Baldeh, Director of the Bank's Transition States Coordination Office .
"Climate action in Africa cannot succeed if it bypasses the places where risks are greatest," added  Anthony Nyong, Director of the Bank's Climate Change and Green Growth Department . "This report gives us a practical roadmap to make adaptation finance more flexible, better targeted and more effective."
Countries facing these pressures share that view. "'Do no harm' is a cardinal principle. But what about 'do good'?" said  Liban Dahir Obsiye, Executive Director of Somalia's National Climate Fund . "We must be proactive in designing projects that involve communities and build resilience at the community level."
From recommendations to action
The report sets out five strategic recommendations:
make conflict prevention and peace explicit co-objectives of climate and development finance
turn integrated climate, conflict and displacement data into early warning and anticipatory action
deploy flexible, risk-tolerant and blended finance tailored to fragile settings
strengthen institutional capacity and project preparation
connect regional cooperation with locally owned delivery
Eight priority actions put these recommendations into practice. Within the Bank, they will inform the forthcoming Climate Change and Green Growth Action Plan and the implementation of the 17th replenishment of the African Development Fund. This builds on more than US$29 billion in climate finance since 2016, including more than US$1.8 billion for fragile settings through the Bank's Transition Support Facility.
original_payload.original_summary: [African Development Bank (AfDB)] Climate and development finance for Africa's fragile and conflict-affected settings must be designed from the outset to prevent conflict and strengthen social cohesion.

original_payload.original_body:
Child marriage is often seen as a women's issue, yet men are key decision-makers and gatekeepers of the norms that sustain it. To end the practice, fathers, traditional leaders and communities must become active allies in protecting girls' rights and futures.
For many families, a wedding celebrates love, commitment and hope. But when one of the people at the altar is a child, we must ask: what exactly are we celebrating? As a mother of two daughters, aged 15 and 16, I want them to finish their education, pursue their ambitions and make their own choices about relationships and parenthood. If our daughters deserve these opportunities, so does every girl.

items.title: Agadez : 68 candidats affrontent les épreuves physiques du concours direct de recrutement des cadres des Eaux et Forêts

original_payload.original_title: Agadez : 68 candidats affrontent les épreuves physiques du concours direct de recrutement des cadres des Eaux et Forêts
original_payload.original_body:
Agadez, 28 Novembre (ANP) – Le Secrétaire Général du Gouvernorat d’Agadez, M. Souleymane Saidou Boulhassane a lancé, ce  samedi  28 Novembre 2026, les épreuves physiques du concours direct de recrutement des Agents du cadre des Eaux et Forêts.
La cérémonie s’est déroulée en présence de l’administrateur délégué de la commune urbaine d’Agadez, du directeur régional de l’Environnement et de la Lutte contre la désertification, ainsi que des responsables des Forces de défense et de sécurité.
Les candidats doivent parcourir, pour les hommes, une distance de 6 kilomètres en 36 minutes, et pour les femmes, une distance de 3 kilomètres en 25 minutes.
A cette occasion, le Secrétaire Général du Gouvernorat d’Agadez a précisé « pour la région d’Agadez, 68 candidats ont répondu présents à l’épreuve physique, dont 55 garçons et 13 filles ».
Il a souligné  que  ce concours vise à recruter 1 000 agents du corps des eaux et forêts pour l’ensemble du territoire national.
« Ceux qui respecteront le temps imparti seront ensuite orientés vers le centre unique de Niamey pour passer l’épreuve écrite. Cette année, un seul centre d’examen est prévu à Niamey », a-t-il informé.
A la fin des épreuves, le Secrétaire Général du Gouvernorat d’Agadez a indiqué que « nous sommes venus les encourager, leur prodiguer quelques conseils d’usage et les inviter à respecter leur rythme ».
NAK/KPM/ANP-282 Novembre 2026

items.title: Aliou Sow, éditeur jeunesse guinéen : «Il faut une politique des livres»

original_payload.original_title: Aliou Sow, éditeur jeunesse guinéen : «Il faut une politique des livres»
original_payload.original_body:
Le grand invité Afrique
Aliou Sow, éditeur jeunesse guinéen : «Il faut une politique des livres»
Publié le :  28/11/2026 - 08:35
Écouter - 07:05
À Montreuil, en banlieue parisienne, le Salon du Livre et de la Presse Jeunesse se poursuit tout le weekend ! Dans les couloirs de cet événement tentaculaire, depuis deux ans, se trouve un Espace Afrique où se réunissent de nombreuses maisons d'édition du continent. Parmi elles, Ganndal, fondée il y a 35 ans par l'éditeur guinéen Aliou Sow avec un mot d'ordre : rendre plus accessibles les livres et la lecture aux jeunes Guinéens.
L'éditeur guinéen Aliou Sow, directeur général et cofondateur des éditions Ganndal.        © éditions ganndal
Publicité
RFI : Aliou Sow, bonjour. Vous êtes présent cette année au Salon du Livre et de la Presse Jeunesse de Montreuil, avec votre maison d'édition Ganndal. Que représente ce salon, pour une maison d'édition comme la vôtre ?
Le Salon de Montreuil peut être considéré comme la plus grosse plateforme de littérature de jeunesse dans l'espace francophone, ou en tout cas l'une des plus grosses, il est important que nous soyons là. Parce que nos maisons d'édition jeunesse africaine sont très peu connues, malheureusement. Nos catalogues ne circulent pas beaucoup, nos auteurs non plus. Donc si nous les éditeurs, nous ne sommes pas là et qu'on se fasse voir et qu'on se fasse prévaloir, le problème va toujours demeurer. Ce qui va avec, c'est que vu toutes les difficultés de distribution et de diffusion de nos livres vers le nord francophone, en France notamment, Belgique, Suisse, etc., le fait de nous rapprocher ici permet aussi de faire savoir que nous sommes prêts à partager avec les distributeurs et les diffuseurs, en tout cas pour ceux qui ne nous connaissent pas jusqu'ici.
Précisément, quels sont les défis auxquels l'édition jeunesse fait face, en Guinée et plus largement en Afrique de l'Ouest ?
Un des défis majeurs, c'est vraiment l'accès aux sources de financement. On est bien d'accord que le livre est un objet culturel, mais c'est aussi un objet commercial, pour lequel on paye pour la fabrication, la distribution, la promotion, etc. Or, la majorité des maisons d'édition ont très peu d'accès à des sources efficaces et solides de financement.
L'autre défi, qui demeure l'un des plus importants, c'est le défi de la distribution. La circulation des livres n'est pas aisée parce que les moyens de transport sont ce qu'ils sont, que les réseaux de librairies sont faiblement développés et qu'il y a peu de diffuseurs professionnalisés et orientés jeunesse.
Pour venir à bout de ces défis, estimez-vous que les États devraient s'impliquer plus dans la circulation des livres, et notamment des livres jeunesse en Afrique de l'Ouest ?
C'est sûr ! Pour ce qui est de la distribution, l'un des grands problèmes que l'on a, c'est que même si des textes régissent la circulation des personnes et des biens - et qui sont théoriquement très volontaristes -, dans la pratique, les entraves demeurent. Pour faire circuler un livre entre la Guinée et la Côte d'Ivoire, c'est un problème. Entre le Mali et le Niger ? Un problème. À l'intérieur des pays eux-mêmes, faire circuler des livres d'une ville X à une ville Y, au sein d'un même pays francophone, ce n'est pas évident.
Donc, ce que les États doivent et peuvent faire, c'est vraiment de travailler entre leurs différents ministères de la culture, pour faciliter la mise en place des politiques publiques du livre et de la lecture.
Les pays anglophones sont beaucoup plus avancés dans cette dynamique, mais malheureusement de ce côté, pour ce qui est des pays francophones, on est très en retard.
Vous défendez une forme de panafricanisme du livre : vous avez noué des partenariats avec des maisons d'édition au Mali, au Togo, en Côte d'Ivoire, au Bénin. Pourquoi ces partenariats sont-ils importants et même essentiels pour la survie des maisons d'édition ?
Le premier objectif, c'est de faciliter la circulation du livre. Nous produisons des coéditions internationales africaines à cinq, ou six, répartis sur plusieurs pays d'Afrique francophone - aussi bien de l'Ouest que de l'Afrique centrale. Le résultat, c'est que le même livre, produit avec des auteurs et des illustrateurs guinéens, va circuler aisément. Car il y a un éditeur dans chacun de ces pays, qui est propriétaire et se sent intéressé à diffuser et à commercialiser ce livre.
Le deuxième objectif, c'est la diversification des catalogues. Il y a un aspect auquel je tiens beaucoup, c'est l'utilisation des langues nationales.
C'est pour ça que nous avons des coéditions de livres bilingues. Ganndal a sorti pour la première fois un livre en quatre langues, du français, du pular, du malinké et du sousou. Du coup, le même livre peut être lu dans toutes les régions de la Guinée sur des déclinaisons de langue nationale.
De plus en plus, on travaille aussi avec quelques éditeurs de pays anglophones, des fois quand ils ont des bons titres, dans des langues africaines qui sont parlées dans des pays francophones, comme le haoussa. Les deux termes clés, ce sont la coédition et la codiffusion.
Au SLPJ, l'un des objectifs est la démocratisation de l'accès à la lecture - car on dit qu'en France, les jeunes lisent moins qu'avant. Est-ce le cas en Guinée ?
Oui, je crois que c'est un phénomène mondial. Mais c'est vrai aussi que pour lire plus, il faut avoir de quoi lire. Et nous, les éditeurs, les francophones en particulier, on s'investit là-dedans. Aujourd'hui, la plupart des livres jeunesse de notre catalogue sont disponibles sur format papier, format numérique, format audio, mais aussi de plus en plus en format accessible en braille - on ne peut pas laisser certains enfants derrière.
Le numérique dont vous parlez peut-il, justement, faciliter l'accès aux livres et à la lecture en Afrique de l'Ouest ?
Absolument. Le téléphone portable, en particulier, est accessible aux enfants dès l'école primaire et au sein des familles. Ce support doit donc être investi par toutes les structures qui travaillent dans le domaine de la lecture. Le numérique sert aussi à ça : qu'il soit disponible sur des plateformes accessibles aux jeunes, pour qu'ils puissent s'adonner à la lecture-plaisir, qui est le plus important à cibler. Ce ne sont pas les manuels scolaires qui sont plus ou moins de la lecture « captive », mais c'est de la lecture-plaisir qui peut se dérouler à travers les livres numériques sur des plateformes.
Mais tout cela, encore une fois, nécessite une synchronisation qui ne sera pas possible sans des bonnes politiques du livre et de la lecture.

items.title: Négocier avec le Jnim, la porte de sortie que l'ICG ouvre aux juntes

original_payload.original_title: Négocier avec le Jnim, la porte de sortie que l'ICG ouvre aux juntes
original_payload.original_body:
Le regard de Newton Ahmed Barry
Négocier avec le Jnim, la porte de sortie que l'ICG ouvre aux juntes
Publié le :  28/11/2026 - 10:48
Écouter - 04:30
Le dernier rapport de l'International Crisis Group, publié le 20 novembre, va faire grincer les dents dans l'AES. Dire que la victoire militaire des juntes de l'AES sur le Jnim est hors de portée, c'est enfreindre un tabou. Comment l'ICG est-il parvenu à cette conclusion ?
Ahmed Newton Barry.        © Anthony Ravera / Studio graphique FMM
Publicité
Je vous propose de lire ce rapport à travers une grille : la fenêtre d'Overton. Pour faire passer une idée d’impensable à possible. Le dialogue avec   le Jnim  , passe d'« impensable » à « possible ». En utilisant un élément de langage que les juntes comprennent bien : « le terrain dicte la manœuvre ».
Les juntes se battent contre un ennemi insaisissable. Le Jnim est une fédération de katibas. Tu détruis une katiba à Mondoro, elle renaît à Boulikessi ou à Djibo. Tu tues un chef, un autre, plus jeune, plus radical, le remplace.
Deux : Les juntes ont perdu le renseignement humain. Or sans les populations, tu ne vois pas le Jnim arriver.
Trois : Les juntes n'ont plus d'armée de masse. Elles ont des armées de capitales. Elles peuvent gagner des batailles. Elles ne peuvent pas gagner la guerre. Elles tiennent les villes. Le Jnim, les zones rurales et des villes moyennes sous blocus.
La spécificité du Jnim dans la galaxie Al-Qaïda
Le Jnim est résilient et il a ce que al-Qaïda au Yémen, al-Shebab en Somalie et al-Qaïda centrale n’ont pas ou non plus : un sanctuaire continental. Trois pays, trois frontières poreuses, le Mali, le Burkina, le Niger. Il a une stratégie locale, pas globale. Il ne veut pas frapper Paris ou New York mais gouverner le Sahel et s'évite les foudres d'une éventuelle coalition mondiale. Il exerce une gouvernance de substitution dans les zones rurales. Il n'est pas pressé de prendre Bamako, Niamey ou Ouaga. Il a juste besoin que Bamako, Niamey et Ouaga ne puissent plus gouverner le pays.
Le scénario plausible pour 2027-2029, selon l’ICG, c'est la continuation de l'érosion des pouvoirs militaires, en trois phases :
Phase 1 - Le statu quo armé : les juntes tiennent les capitales, le Jnim, les zones rurales et étrangle l'économie : blocus de villes secondaires, attaques des convois, taxes sur l'or, le bétail, le carburant.
Phase 2 – Accentuation de négociations locales en vue de trêves avec le Jnim pour rouvrir un marché, une école, une route.
Phase 3 – Le choix forcé : une des trois juntes finira par craquer, par épuisement budgétaire, par essoufflement du soutien russe, par fragilité du rapprochement algérien, ou par menace de putsch interne. Celle-là ouvrira un dialogue officiel. Les deux autres suivront, quitte à accuser la première d'avoir trahi.
À cet égard, on peut dire que Crisis Group a eu le nez creux. Alger a brièvement tenté une « intercession » inter-maliens qui a tourné court. Fautes de conditions réunies, dit ATTAF. Parce qu’il n’y avait rien à négocier, rétorque le FLA.
En conclusion : Crisis Group n'offre pas la paix aux juntes, mais des éléments de langage. Le dialogue devient « stratégie » et non « trahison ». Des modèles : la Mauritanie et le Nigeria. Parce que sans cette porte de sortie verbale, les juntes préfèrent mourir les armes à la main, et faire mourir leur pays avec elles, plutôt que d'avouer que le tout-militaire a échoué.

items.title: À la Une: le pouvoir congolais confronté à trois tests de confiance

original_payload.original_title: À la Une: le pouvoir congolais confronté à trois tests de confiance
original_payload.original_body:
La Une de la presse cette semaine à Kinshasa
À la Une: le pouvoir congolais confronté à trois tests de confiance
Publié le :  28/11/2026 - 07:26
Écouter - 03:00
Pascal Mulegwa.        © Anthony Ravera / Studio graphique FMM
Publicité
Église, majorité, voisin ougandais : cette semaine, la presse de Kinshasa raconte un pouvoir confronté à trois tests de confiance. Dans chacun de ces dossiers, les déclarations ne suffisent plus : ce sont désormais les actes qui sont attendus.
«  24 heures que l’Église décrit comme une tyrannie à Kinshasa et Lubumbashi  », titre    Africanews  .
Le trihebdo kinois oppose les explications sécuritaires des autorités aux griefs de la hiérarchie catholique, qui affirme avoir obtenu les autorisations nécessaires et payé les frais exigés. À Kinshasa, la Journée diocésaine des jeunes n’a pas pu se tenir au stade Tata Raphaël. À Lubumbashi, une marche réclamant l’exécution d’une décision de justice sur la concession du Grand Séminaire Saint-Paul a été dispersée aux gaz lacrymogènes.
La Conférence épiscopale nationale du Congo dénonce une «  restriction préoccupante  » de la liberté de culte. «  Gazer les évêques et les paisibles manifestants en prière […] est une forme de tyrannie que notre pays qui se proclame démocratique ne mérite vraiment pas.  » Le tabloïd reprend «  Tyrannie  » et rappelle que le mot est lâché «  par l’institution la plus prudente du pays  » et qui a longtemps privilégié la médiation.
Le quotidien  Le Journal  parle du « temps de l’apaisement »
Après deux épisodes de tension à Kinshasa et à Lubumbashi, le gouvernement congolais multiplie les gestes d’ouverture envers la hiérarchie catholique. Entre impératifs sécuritaires, liberté de culte et respect des décisions judiciaires, l’exécutif est désormais attendu sur le terrain des actes.
Autre sujet : la majorité présidentielle est-elle en train de se fissurer ? «  Union sacrée : Vital Kamerhe amorce sa traversée du désert  », annonce    Congo Nouveau   .
Après Modeste Bahati Lukwebo, c'est au tour de Vital Kamerhe de faire face à une fronde au sein de sa propre famille politique. Ses prises de position sur la gestion financière de la guerre dans l'Est de la RDC ont provoqué un désaveu public de plusieurs cadres de l'Union pour la nation congolaise (UNC). Une situation qui révèle les limites de la liberté de parole au sein de l'Union sacrée de la nation.
La scène politique congolaise semble se répéter, avec des acteurs différents, mais un mécanisme presque identique : celui de la contestation interne contre les responsables politiques qui osent exprimer des réserves sur certaines orientations de la majorité présidentielle.
Révision de la Constitution, Bahati Lukwebo et Vital Kamerhe fragilisés
Après Modeste Bahati Lukwebo, fragilisé au sein de l'Alliance des forces démocratiques du Congo (AFDC) pour ses positions critiques sur le projet de changement ou de révision de la Constitution, Vital Kamerhe se retrouve à son tour confronté à une fronde dans son propre parti.
Cette fois, le désaccord porte sur la conduite de la guerre dans l'Est du pays et, surtout, sur la gestion des ressources financières mobilisées pour répondre à la crise sécuritaire. En soulevant la question de l'efficacité de l'effort de guerre et de la nécessité de rendre compte de l'utilisation des deniers publics, le président national de l'UNC a ouvert un front politique inattendu dans son propre camp.
Onze cadres de l’UNC ont pris leurs distances avec leur président, après ses interrogations sur la gestion financière de l’effort de guerre dans l’Est. Le trihebdomadaire y voit un avertissement : «  la prise de distance avec la ligne dominante peut avoir un coût politique jusque dans sa propre maison  ».
Econews va plus loin avec son titre : «  Après Bahati, Kamerhe dans la tourmente  ». Le trihebdomadaire pose la question d’une majorité présidentielle devenue «  instrument de domination  ». Il estime que l’affaiblissement successif de Modeste Bahati, puis de Vital Kamerhe, pourrait profiter au parti présidentiel UDPS qui veut : «  régner sans partage au sein  » de la majorité. Une recomposition qui interroge  Econews : « Les   alliés   du pouvoir sont-ils encore des partenaires ou deviennent-ils des figurants ?  »
«  Brasier diplomatique  » entre Kinshasa et Kampala
Enfin, les relations avec l’Ouganda restent sous tension. «  Kinshasa ne décolère pas face à Kampala  », titre  Ouragan .
«  Il y a des silences qui tuent et des colères qui sauvent  », lance le trihebdo qui se satisfait de l'option de Kinshasa : la colère gronde face aux tweets venimeux du chef de l'armée ougandaise, Muhoozi Kainerugaba.
En clair, la RDC a décidé d'aller au clash. Mercredi 25 novembre, la ministre des Affaires étrangères, Thérèse Kayikwamba, a convoqué le chef de la mission diplomatique ougandaise en RDC pour lui signifier, sans gants ni détours, qu'on ne joue pas avec la dignité d'un peuple déterminé à ne pas rester téléspectateur face à quiconque veut prendre ne serait-ce qu'un centimètre de sa terre.
La ministre a fustigé le soutien affiché du chef militaire ougandais au mouvement rebelle FRN de Joseph Kabila.
Le journal parle d’un «  brasier diplomatique  ». Le quotidien    Le Potentiel    rappelle que «  la RDC n’est ni une terre sans maître   ni un territoire dont le sort se décide sur les réseaux sociaux ».
Dans  Tempête des tropiques , une mise en garde résume l’enjeu : «  coopération militaire  » ne signifie pas «  confiance stratégique  ».
Au quotidien de conclure : l'Ouganda peut combattre les ADF aux côtés des Congolais sans être un allié inconditionnel dans la crise régionale. Kinshasa attend toujours de Kampala une clarification.

items.title: 2027: PWDs pledge massive turnout

original_payload.original_title: 2027: PWDs pledge massive turnout
original_payload.original_body:
General News  2027: PWDs pledge massive turnout
By  Folasade Akpan   ·   8 seconds ago   ·  3 min read
✓
✓
By Emmanuel Oloniruha
Persons with Disabilities (PWDs) in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) have pledged massive participation in the 2027 general elections following a voter education campaign by TAF Africa.
They made the pledge at the Able2Vote voter education campaign in Abuja.
The campaign was organised by TAF Africa, with support from the European Union Support to Democratic Governance in Nigeria Phase II (EU-SDGN II) Programme.
The campaign which held at the Disabled Colony Centre, Karomajiji, Airport Road, Abuja, sensitised PWDs on their electoral rights, voter registration, Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) collection, accessible voting arrangements, ballot secrecy and how to counter electoral misinformation.
Mr Yakubu Shekwolo, President, FCT Indigenous Persons with Disabilities and a social worker in the Abuja Municipal Area Council (AMAC), said the sensitisation was the first of its kind and had given PWDs a sense of belonging.
“I am the happiest person today to have seen this programme, because for years persons with disabilities have been discriminated from election activities,” Shekwolo said.
He said the education had enlightened many PWDs on how to protect their votes and expressed optimism that with assurance of security from the organisers, PWDs would come out massively in 2027.
Secretary to the Emir of Persons with Disability, FCT, Mr Muhammad Dantani, said the sensitisation was important because it created awareness on new programmes for PWDs.
Dantani said PWDs in the FCT support leaders who cared for them, noting that the APC administration signed the Discrimination Against Persons with Disabilities (Prohibition) Act and established the National Commission for Persons with Disabilities.
“We don’t elect party, we elect person. Any party that wants our support must tell us what it will do for persons with disability.
“If you see ramp in schools here in Karomajiji and in our trade centre, it is because we are being considered. That is what we want in markets, hospitals and banks,” he said.
Speaking on the campaign, Programme Manager, TAF Africa, Dr Andrew Adaji, said the Able2Vote campaign, which had been conducted across the country, was being rounded off in the FCT.
Adaji said teams were deployed to Kuje, Kwali, Karomajiji, Karu and Bwari to identify polling units of PWDs and sensitise them on the forthcoming elections.
He said previous sensitisation during off-cycle elections in Osun, Ekiti and Anambra led to increased participation of PWDs, especially persons with hearing impairment, after provision of sign language interpreters and assistive devices such as Braille ballot guides and magnifying glasses.
“For the 2027 elections, the scope is wider. We are engaging INEC and the Association of Sign Language Interpreters of Nigeria so that where we have voters with hearing impairment, the commission can engage sign language interpreters as ad hoc staff,” he said.
Adaji added that TAF Africa had engaged the Police and the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) on inclusive policing to prioritise PWDs during election-day mobility challenges and violence.
According to him, the Able2Vote campaign seeks to ensure that disability does not become a barrier to electoral participation and that PWDs have access to electoral information, voter registration services and polling units without discrimination.(NAN)

items.title: AI to transform workplace skills, talent development – Adogbo

original_payload.original_title: AI to transform workplace skills, talent development – Adogbo
original_payload.original_body:
Science & Tech  AI to transform workplace skills, talent development – Adogbo
By  Philip Daniel Yatai   ·   1 hour ago   ·  5 min read
✓
✓
By Edith Tsokar
‎
‎An expert, Mr Gideon Adogbo says Artificial Intelligence (AI) will significantly reshape the workplace, requiring organisations to rethink talent development and workforce capabilities.
Adogbo,‌‍‌‍⁠‍⁠⁠‍⁠⁠‌‍‍‌ Senior Technical Adviser on Reform Technology and Innovation to the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation, disclosed this at the 2026 Strategists’ Forum of the Institute of Strategic Management of Nigeria (ISMN) on Friday in Abuja.
He spoke on the theme, “Strategy, Technology and Talent: The Tripod for a Future-Ready Organisation,” highlighting the need for organisations to align strategic leadership, technological innovation and human capabilities.
According to him, technological advancement is changing the traditional understanding of intelligence, skills and professional expertise, making it necessary for organisations to prepare their employees for emerging workplace realities.
“Talent has become the capability of combined organisations. It includes intelligence, skill, expertise and authority,” he said.
Adogbo explained that AI was increasingly capable of acquiring and deploying skills previously associated with human professionals, thereby changing the relationship between technology and human labour.
He said the future workplace would increasingly consist of both human employees and intelligent technological agents, stressing that organisations must understand how to manage the emerging combination.
“The future organisation will no longer be only human beings. It will be humans and machines, agents,” he said.
The expert noted that routine professional skills could increasingly be replicated through AI, reducing the exclusivity of certain competencies and requiring workers to develop new areas of value.
“There are some skills you have, but AI will learn them from you. The skills you have today, which you pride yourself on, AI will learn and translate to every other person,” he said.
He, however, identified authority and decision-making as important considerations in the evolving relationship between humans and technology, particularly in determining who should exercise control over critical organisational decisions.
“Are we preparing people for the work we have done, or are we preparing them for the future?” he asked.
Adogbo also observed that access to intelligence and technological resources was becoming increasingly widespread, reducing the competitive advantage previously associated with specialised knowledge and language proficiency.
According to him, organisations must develop clear strategies that identify the value they intend to create, the people they seek to serve and the capabilities required to achieve their objectives.
He said strategy should provide organisational direction and establish priorities, while technology should support the delivery of measurable results.
Adogbo illustrated organisational performance and adaptability using the analogy of a tripod, explaining that strategy, technology and talent must work together without any weak link.
According to him, technology alone does not guarantee value if organisational priorities are unclear or poorly aligned.
He noted that while strategy defines how value is created and how resources are prioritised, strong strategies could still fail during execution if talent was inadequate or the working environment was unsupportive.
Adogbo added that leadership, culture, trust and accountability were essential enablers that tied strategy, talent and technology together, stressing that intentionality was required rather than merely putting plans on paper.
He said intentional strategy and people-centric leadership remained key to winning business, attracting international investment and staying competitive.
Earlier, Mr Alex Enebeli, the President and Chairman of the Council of ISMN, said the institute’s 21st Forum charter was designed to prepare public servants within Grade Levels 14 to 17 for strategic leadership and professional management responsibilities.
He said the institute was working towards implementing the mandate through strategic management programmes tailored to ministries, departments and agencies.
According to him, the initiative would also extend to the private sector, civil society organisations, security, cybersecurity, healthcare, artificial intelligence and environmental, social and governance-related areas.
“Our institute is unique because we receive everyone from every background. We add value to you, so you are ready for a lifestyle of strategy and leadership,” he said.
The ISMN president said the institute was strengthening partnerships with universities, polytechnics and colleges within and outside Nigeria to align academic curricula with professional competencies.
He explained that the partnerships were aimed at creating stronger pathways between academic qualifications and professional development, stressing that leadership and strategic management skills were necessary across all professions.
Enebeli said the institute had secured approval from its Governing Board to organise an International Strategies Forum in November 2027.
He said the proposed forum would feature masterclasses, professional development programmes, membership induction, exhibitions and specialised programmes for fellows, among other activities.
The president further said the institute was expanding its international collaborations and postgraduate programmes through partnerships with universities and business schools.
Dr Nura Umar, the Director-General of the National Information Technology Development Agency (NITDA), said the forum’s theme aligned with the agency’s strategic priorities, particularly its commitment to expanding digital literacy in Nigeria.
Umar, represented by Dr Ayodeji Eniola, Director of Corporate Planning and Strategy, NITDA, said the agency had been implementing its Strategic Roadmap and Action Plan 2.0, which included an ambition to ensure that 70 per cent of Nigerians acquired digital literacy by 2027.
Umar said technology remained essential to national development, adding that strategic management, technological advancement and talent development were interconnected.(NAN)

items.title: Researcher warns eclampsia could kill 1 in 4 affected women

original_payload.original_title: Researcher warns eclampsia could kill 1 in 4 affected women
original_payload.original_body:
General News  Researcher warns eclampsia could kill 1 in 4 affected women
By  Tosin Kolade   ·   3 hours ago   ·  3 min read
✓
✓
By Kemi Akintokun
A medical researcher, Dr Aigbe Ohihoin, has warned that eclampsia could cause the death of one in four affected women, underscoring the need for improved maternal healthcare.
Ohihoin, Director of Maternal and Reproductive Health Research at the Nigerian Institute of Medical Research (NIMR), gave the warning in Lagos on Thursday.
He spoke at the institute’s 15th inaugural lecture, titled: ‘All for the Woman, Her Baby and Her Health.’
The consultant obstetrician and gynaecologist identified postpartum haemorrhage, eclampsia and pre-eclampsia as major causes of maternal deaths requiring urgent attention.
He explained that pre-eclampsia was associated with high blood pressure during pregnancy, while eclampsia involved seizures that could endanger the lives of both mother and baby.
Ohihoin said findings from his published research indicated a 25 per cent mortality rate among women affected by eclampsia.
“These conditions are deadly. Some women might not know they have it until high blood pressure is detected during antenatal visits,” he said.
He identified headaches and blurred vision as other warning signs, noting that the condition could have progressed significantly before such symptoms appeared.
The researcher said maternal mortality resulted from both direct and indirect causes, compounded by socioeconomic factors.
He listed educational background, access to information, infrastructure and the responsiveness of healthcare systems to emergencies as factors influencing maternal deaths.
Ohihoin called for increased investment in women’s education and financial empowerment to enable them to make informed decisions and access quality healthcare.
“Women need to access health information. And that information will empower them to make the right choices, make the right decisions.
“A healthy woman is a healthy family. A healthy family is a healthy nation. That’s why we must ensure that the woman is healthy,” he said.
He stressed the link between maternal and child wellbeing, advocating policies that prioritised women’s health, reproductive rights, choices and aspirations.
Ohihoin said women should not be viewed merely as vessels for childbearing, adding that their wellbeing extended beyond motherhood and their roles as sexual partners.
He said his commitment to women’s education and reproductive rights was partly influenced by his mother’s experience of interrupting her education to raise him.
According to him, motherhood should not compel women to abandon their educational aspirations or sacrifice personal development.
“A society that values women must create families, services and policies that allow women to care for others without sacrificing their own development,” he said.
On NIMR’s interventions, Ohihoin said Nigeria had recorded progress in preventing mother-to-child transmission of HIV.
He disclosed that no transmission was recorded among the cohorts monitored by the institute.
He attributed the achievement to public health interventions, government support, development partners’ funding and the contributions of healthcare workers.
He acknowledged the support of the U.S. President’s Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR) and the Nigerian Government in preventing mother-to-child transmission.
However, Ohihoin called for increased investment in medical research, saying current funding for research activities and capacity development in Nigeria was inadequate.
He urged Nigerians to recognise women’s contributions to society and support initiatives promoting their health, quality of life and advancement.
The researcher also advocated equal treatment of male and female children, expressing concern over couples seeking sex selection because of their preference for male children.   (NAN)
Edited by Kamal Oropo

items.title: Nnaji unveils Enugu manifesto, promises 50,000 jobs, industrialisation

original_payload.original_title: Nnaji unveils Enugu manifesto, promises 50,000 jobs, industrialisation
original_payload.original_body:
General News  Nnaji unveils Enugu manifesto, promises 50,000 jobs, industrialisation
By  Tosin Kolade   ·   3 hours ago   ·  2 min read
✓
✓
By Ifeoma Aka
The Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate in Enugu State, Chief Uche Nnaji, has unveiled a manifesto centred on economic recovery, industrialisation and job creation.
Nnaji unveiled the manifesto on Friday in Enugu during the inauguration of the party’s Campaign Directorate.
The former Minister of Science and Technology urged members of the campaign directorate to mobilise support for his governorship ambition.
He named Chief Charles Ndikwe, former Managing Director of Rangers International Club, as Director-General of the campaign.
Nnaji said the manifesto was built around five pillars: open governance, security and public safety, economic development, agriculture and food security.
He said the document provided a practical framework for addressing the state’s challenges, adding that his campaign would focus on realistic commitments rather than promises that could not be fulfilled.
The candidate said his proposed administration would prioritise youth development and job creation, with a target of generating 50,000 direct and indirect jobs through industrial development.
He expressed concern over what he called the declining economic fortunes of the state, arguing that increased government revenue had not translated into improved prosperity for residents.
“What we are doing is giving a manifesto based on truth and reality, not a manifesto based on lies.
“When we build these industries, we will be able to take a minimum of 50,000 youths off the streets through direct and indirect employment.
“We want to have a society where there will be no danger to people’s lives. We want to wipe out or drastically reduce hunger in this state,” he said.
Nnaji also expressed concern over the state of the middle class in Enugu, saying the population was increasingly divided between the rich and the poor.
He pledged to serve only one four-year term, which he said would be sufficient to establish a new development foundation for the state.
He also promised a four-year tax-free period, reduced rents and school fees, as well as free medical treatment for residents aged 70 and above at a dedicated hospital.
“We are going to follow this manifesto to the letter,” he said.
Nnaji assured members of the campaign council of his willingness to work with them to implement the party’s development agenda.
He urged them to commit themselves to mobilising support for the governorship campaign.   (NAN)
Edited by Maureen Atuonwu

items.title: Foundation seeks stronger laws, shelters to tackle femicide

original_payload.original_title: Foundation seeks stronger laws, shelters to tackle femicide
original_payload.original_body:
General News  Foundation seeks stronger laws, shelters to tackle femicide
By  Tosin Kolade   ·   3 hours ago   ·  3 min read
✓
✓
By Kemi Akintokun
The DOHS Cares Foundation has called for stronger legal protection, increased funding for shelters and improved support systems to address femicide in Nigeria.
The foundation’s founder, Mrs Ololade Ajayi, made the call at the International Summit on Voices Against Femicide, held on Nov. 27 at the German Bundestag in Berlin.
Ajayi, who represented Nigeria, presented findings from the foundation’s 2025 and 2026 Nigeria Femicide Reports and advocated the enactment of a dedicated Femicide Prevention Law.
The summit, hosted by Die Linke in the Bundestag, brought together parliamentarians, activists, researchers and experts from more than 15 countries to discuss strategies for addressing femicide and gender-based violence.
Ajayi highlighted cases of women and girls allegedly killed by intimate partners, former partners and acquaintances, with some incidents reportedly covered up by family members.
She identified gaps in Nigeria’s response, including the absence of a standalone law recognising femicide as a distinct crime and fewer than 50 functioning shelters for survivors of gender-based violence.
The advocate said the gaps required stronger institutional measures, considering Nigeria’s population of more than 220 million.
She also highlighted the foundation’s advocacy initiatives, including a draft Femicide Bill submitted to the National Assembly and a proposed PreFem App for early warning and reporting of threats.
Ajayi urged governments to treat femicide as a public safety emergency, fund shelters, train police officers and judges, and establish a global database on gender-related killings.
“Femicide is not just a Nigerian problem; it is a global emergency. I am honoured to bring the voices of Nigerian women, the living and the dead, to the heart of the German Parliament.
“We came to Berlin to learn, but also to teach: that without data, law, shelters and political will, women will keep dying. Nigeria must act, and the world must act with us,” she said.
At the summit, a Member of Parliament, Kathy Gebel, thanked lawmakers who supported the event, particularly Cansu Ozdemir.
Gebel said the discussions had provided fresh perspectives on addressing violence against women, noting that progress in securing women’s rights had come through sustained advocacy.
She urged participants to translate ideas from the summit into practical action to strengthen women’s rights and protection.
The summit came amid renewed calls in Germany for stronger laws, school-based prevention programmes and expanded shelters for women, following a minute of silence by the Bundestag for femicide victims on Nov. 25, observed as Orange Day.
The event also coincided with the 16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence.
(NAN)

items.title: Women outnumber men in Raja county voter registration

original_payload.original_title: Women outnumber men in Raja county voter registration
original_payload.original_body:
Women accounted for more than half of the 9,428 people registered to vote in Raja County, Western Bahr el Ghazal State, between November 18 and 25, according to local election officials.
Figures released by the county election office showed that 5,277 women and 4,151 men had registered during the period.
Raja County is a remote area of northwestern South Sudan bordering Sudan.
Wahby Musa Hassan, assistant returning officer of the State High Election Committee in Raja County, confirmed the figures in an interview with Radio Tamazuj on Thursday.
He said the figures were based on daily reports from 14 accessible registration centres, while reports from another 19 centres had yet to reach the county office because of poor network connectivity and long distances.
Hassan attributed the higher number of female registrants to public awareness and mobilisation campaigns led by women-focused organisations in the area.
He identified transport difficulties, poor network connectivity and shortages of essential registration equipment as major challenges facing the exercise, particularly in remote payams.
These included shortages of vehicles, lamination machines and other registration materials.
“We do not have a vehicle, and we also lack lamination machines. However, we are grateful that we have managed to overcome some of these challenges. Today, some supplies will arrive from Wau, including a lamination machine,” he said.
Hassan said the election commission was carrying out its responsibilities independently under the Election Act, with cooperation from local government departments.
He urged eligible citizens, including women, men, young people, political leaders, security personnel, business communities, traditional leaders and political parties, to use the remaining days to register.
“We are targeting a large number of registered voters, and I encourage everyone to come forward and register. We have only a limited time remaining, and those who do not register will miss the opportunity to exercise their right to vote,” he said.
He said elections offer citizens an opportunity to choose their leaders through the ballot and participate in shaping the country’s future.
Hassan added that the next stage would involve displaying the provisional voters’ register to allow citizens to verify their details and request corrections before the elections.
Voter registration is scheduled to close on Saturday, November 28. However, registration centres in Wau town remained congested on Saturday morning, with hundreds of people waiting to register.
South Sudan’s general elections are scheduled for February 11, 2027, under the revised timetable announced by the National Elections Commission.

items.title: Excluded Lakes aspirant expresses disappointment, urges SPLM reforms

original_payload.original_title: Excluded Lakes aspirant expresses disappointment, urges SPLM reforms
original_payload.original_body:
A former police officer who resigned to pursue politics has criticised his exclusion from the race for Lakes State governor under the ruling SPLM, alleging political interference and calling for reforms to strengthen internal democracy.
Gen. Manguen Dut Manguen told Radio Tamazuj on Thursday that he had campaigned across Lakes State and was confident of competing in the party’s gubernatorial primaries before being summoned and informed that he would no longer participate.
He said he was summoned alongside two other aspirants, David Nok Marial and Muor-Anyar, to the SPLM Secretariat, where they met Deputy Chairman Simon Kun Puoc, Secretary-General Akol Paul Koordit and the chairperson of the party’s Primaries and Congresses Committee, David Yau Yau.
Manguen said he asked why he had been excluded but was told he had done nothing wrong and could instead be appointed to a government position in Juba.
“I asked them what my issue was and what I had done against the nation or the party. The Secretary-General, Akol Paul Koordit, responded that I had done nothing wrong but that I would soon be appointed to a ministry or another government position in Juba,” he said.
He questioned why he was being offered an appointment instead of being allowed to contest, saying he had been an SPLM member for 26 years and had received no explanation for his exclusion.
“I asked him what had disqualified me, but he told me there was nothing against me. He simply asked me to accept his decision,” Manguen said.
Political rivalry
Manguen alleged that internal political rivalry may have influenced his exclusion, suggesting that his gubernatorial ambitions could have threatened Koordit’s position because both men come from Rumbek Centre.
“He may have been protecting his position because he knew that if I remained in the race and won the governorship, he could lose his position,” he alleged.
Radio Tamazuj could not independently verify the allegation.
Despite his disappointment, Manguen said he would remain in the SPLM and continue supporting the party.
“I have been a member of this party for 26 years, and I will remain an SPLM member. I will continue serving the party in any capacity required,” he said.
He said he had travelled from Rumbek to Yirol and was returning to Juba to avoid possible tensions following his exclusion.
Community projects
Manguen said he would not seek reimbursement for campaign expenses, adding that he had donated boreholes to communities in four counties.
He said four boreholes each had been allocated to Wulu and Rumbek North, and two each to Yirol East and Rumbek East, but remained stranded at the Nimule border because of outstanding taxes and clearance costs.
He said he was considering selling a plot of land to raise money to transport the equipment to the communities.
Manguen said he would continue fulfilling development commitments made during his campaign, insisting that residents should not suffer because of his exclusion.
Security and development
He said his bid for the governorship position was driven by a desire to improve security and development in Lakes State, arguing that insecurity should not be used to justify neglecting public services or misuse of public resources.
“People should not continue hiding behind the issue of security while development is neglected. Security cannot be used as an umbrella under which public resources are looted,” he said.
He argued that investment in businesses, factories and other economic activities could create jobs, reduce competition over resources and help address local conflicts.
Call for reforms
Manguen urged the SPLM to strengthen its internal structures and selection procedures, saying party members should have a fair opportunity to compete for leadership positions.
He thanked President Salva Kiir Mayardit and the party leadership for providing opportunities for members to participate in selecting leaders but said internal processes needed greater transparency and accountability.
“What I am suggesting is that the SPLM should be properly revived and strengthened, regardless of whether the current leadership is doing well or not. I am not accusing anyone, but this is what I believe needs to be addressed,” he said.

items.title: Remote voters risk missing registration deadline in Eastern Equatoria

original_payload.original_title: Remote voters risk missing registration deadline in Eastern Equatoria
original_payload.original_body:
Eligible voters in remote communities in South Sudan’s Eastern Equatoria State risk missing the voter registration deadline because of delayed delivery of materials, inadequate civic education and long distances to registration centres, civil society representatives have warned.
With registration due to close on Saturday, civil society groups are urging the National Election Commission (NEC) to extend the exercise, saying logistical challenges have prevented many residents in remote areas from registering.
David Nayee Lomor, caretaker commissioner of Kapoeta North County, told Radio Tamazuj that registration in the county began about five days late.
He said all registration materials had since reached the county’s 28 designated centres and that registration teams had been deployed.
Lomor attributed the delay to possible technical and transportation challenges, including the movement of materials from Juba to Torit before distribution to the counties.
He said the registration period was too short and called on the NEC to allow more time.
“We wish that the National Election Commission could have not put a deadline so fast,” he said.
Christine Athom, civil society coordinator for Lafon at the Civil Society Response for Development Organization, said inadequate civic education and late delivery of registration materials had hampered participation in remote communities.
She said awareness campaigns had failed to reach many residents before registration began.
“The community lacks awareness because the civic education has not reached them at all levels from the beginning,” she said.
Athom said some registration teams in Lafon received materials on Thursday and Friday, several days after the exercise began on Monday.
She warned that many eligible residents could miss the deadline because of the delays.
“The remaining time will not be enough because at the moment most of the people have not registered,” she said.
Athom urged the NEC and the State Election Commission to extend registration, saying residents in remote areas needed more time to access the centres.
She also raised concerns about people living far from registration centres, particularly persons with physical disabilities and visual impairments, who face additional barriers to accessing registration services.
She called for greater cooperation between government institutions and civil society organisations to expand civic education and reach communities in villages and payams.
“If they are leaving out the civil society organizations, then that is the gap that we have,” she said.
In Kapoeta North, all 28 designated registration centres have received materials, according to Lomor, despite the reported five-day delay in starting the exercise.
The registration exercise is due to close on Saturday, November 28. South Sudan is scheduled to hold general elections on February 11, 2027.

items.title: South Sudan youth groups call for greater representation

original_payload.original_title: South Sudan youth groups call for greater representation
original_payload.original_body:
Youth-led organisations in South Sudan on Friday called for greater representation in government, saying young people remain underrepresented in leadership and decision-making positions.
Florence Agiba, executive director of youth-led organisation Markaz Al-Salam, said findings from a recent assessment showed little improvement in youth representation compared with last year, despite progress in some states.
“Looking at what happened last year and this year, I can say the similarity is that youth in leadership is still low,” Agiba said.
She cited Unity State, where four young people had been appointed as ministers, as an example of relatively higher youth representation. Central Equatoria State also recorded higher youth representation in last year’s assessment, she said.
Agiba said the latest assessment did not include members of parliament because the country currently has no legislature in place. In the previous assessment, young people accounted for about 4.81% of parliamentarians, representing approximately 23 of the 550 members.
She said Markaz Al-Salam, with support from Norwegian People’s Aid (NPA) and in collaboration with the National Youth Union, was preparing a simplified fact sheet to share the findings and support advocacy for increased youth participation.
Agiba urged young people to participate in the forthcoming elections and support candidates from their generation.
“We want to see more and more young people take up leadership roles. Those that are out there, please vote for these positions. And those that are not vying, please vote for our own young people,” she said.
She called for youth representation to reach at least 20%, saying young people should have a greater role in shaping the country’s future.
Meanwhile, Michael Gorjin Kuol, NPA’s project manager, urged youth organisations to sustain advocacy efforts by engaging political parties and government institutions on the need for greater youth participation.
He proposed a high-level dialogue involving young people, political parties, the Political Parties Council and the National Elections Commission to discuss barriers to youth participation in leadership.
Kuol said the assessment findings should be simplified and disseminated through newspapers, radio stations and social media to ensure young people and communities across the country could access the information.
He also encouraged youth organisations to establish a mechanism for regularly documenting and monitoring appointments of young people to government positions.
Counsel Izale Benjamin, popularly known as Yaba.com, said limited awareness of the National Youth Policy was among the factors preventing young people from demanding greater participation in decision-making.
He said the policy provides for 20% youth representation at different levels of government, but many young people are unaware of the provision.
“I believe they are not aware,” Benjamin said, calling for public awareness campaigns to educate young people about their rights and encourage them to participate in national development.
Benjamin urged young people to focus on nation-building, acquire vocational skills and participate peacefully in politics rather than engage in communal conflicts.
Youth organisations say greater representation in government is essential to ensuring young people contribute to decisions affecting South Sudan’s future.

items.title: Mandoul : le comité de pilotage du projet LAPIA évalue les avancées en matière de cohésion sociale

original_payload.original_title: Mandoul : le comité de pilotage du projet LAPIA évalue les avancées en matière de cohésion sociale
original_payload.original_body:
Le comité de pilotage du projet LAPIA (Soutien à la cohésion sociale et à la cohabitation pacifique dans le Sud du Tchad) a tenu une rencontre à Koumra du 25 au 26 novembre.
Cette réunion a rassemblé les représentants des trois provinces bénéficiaires du projet, notamment le Logone oriental, le Mandoul et le Moyen-Chari.
Autorités administratives des trois provinces, chefs des services déconcentrés provinciaux concernés, autorités traditionnelles et religieuses, associations des jeunes et des femmes ainsi que les membres du consortium ont pris part à ces assises.
Prenant la parole au nom du président du comité de pilotage, Djikoloum Ndouba a expliqué que le choix de Koumra pour abriter cette rencontre n’est pas fortuit.
Il traduit, selon lui, la volonté de rapprocher le comité des communautés et de leurs réalités quotidiennes, notamment les conflits entre agriculteurs et éleveurs, la gestion pacifique du foncier, la préservation de l’harmonie au sein des institutions coutumières ainsi que l’accès équitable aux ressources naturelles.
Il a également souligné l’importance de cette étape dans la mise en œuvre du projet, qui accompagne techniquement et financièrement 35 organisations locales engagées dans la promotion de la paix au sein de leurs communautés.
« C’est là toute l’âme de l’approche de LAPIA : confier aux acteurs locaux eux-mêmes le soin de bâtir la paix, car nul ne connaît mieux que les communautés les chemins de leur propre réconciliation », a-t-il déclaré.
Lire aussi  :  Mandoul : fin de la tournée de sensibilisation du sous-préfet de Bessada sur la cohésion sociale et le développement local
Pour sa part, la chargée de programme de COGINTA, Mireille Widmer, a salué les efforts du consortium composé d’ARED, RESAP.MC, CARITAS Goré et CRASH. Elle a reconnu le travail accompli par ces organisations en faveur du renforcement de la cohésion sociale et de la prévention des conflits, dans des contextes souvent sensibles.
Intervenant à son tour, la cheffe de la section gouvernance de la délégation de l’Union européenne au Tchad, Agnès Kovacs, a rappelé que le projet entre dans sa dernière année de mise en œuvre. Elle a, à cet effet, insisté sur la nécessité de consolider les résultats obtenus et de garantir la pérennisation des acquis afin que les actions engagées puissent continuer à produire des effets au-delà de la durée du projet.
Dans son allocution, le Délégué général du gouvernement auprès de la province du Mandoul, Ahmat Abdallah Fadoul a salué l’initiative du projet LAPIA, qui intervient dans un domaine essentiel pour la stabilité et le développement des communautés.
Il a souligné que la cohésion sociale et la cohabitation pacifique constituent des conditions indispensables à la préservation de la paix et au renforcement du vivre-ensemble.
L’occasion pour l’autorité de révéler que les conflits liés à l’exploitation des ressources naturelles, notamment entre agriculteurs et éleveurs, ainsi que les différends fonciers, représentent des défis auxquels les autorités administratives, traditionnelles et les communautés doivent faire face collectivement.
À cet effet, il a encouragé les organisations locales bénéficiaires du projet à poursuivre leurs efforts de sensibilisation, de médiation et de prévention des conflits. Il a par ailleurs invité les différentes parties prenantes à privilégier le dialogue, la concertation et le règlement pacifique des différends.
Pour terminer, il a réaffirmé l’engagement des autorités provinciales à accompagner toutes les initiatives visant à consolider la paix, la stabilité et la cohésion sociale dans le Mandoul et dans les autres provinces concernées.
À travers cette rencontre, le comité de pilotage entend ainsi faire le point sur les réalisations, apprécier les avancées enregistrées et renforcer les stratégies d’intervention des organisations, consolider les mécanismes communautaires de prévention et de gestion pacifique des conflits.
Cette rencontre constitue donc une étape importante pour inscrire durablement les acquis du projet LAPIA dans les pratiques locales et faire de la cohésion sociale un levier essentiel du vivre-ensemble et de la paix dans les provinces du Sud du Tchad.
Alex Loubadjo Djassibaye
